summary: Lake County, MN: a 100-foot steel tower near Kekekabic Lake, completed 1937, staffed by one observer from 1939; toppled by the 1970s and now listed as gone; the site is in the Boundary Waters wilderness.

facts.design: 100-foot steel tower with a square cab; radio only, no telephone line
facts.status_note: FFLA lists it as gone; a Minnesota list says it is no longer standing and was probably damaged during removal; a visitor found it toppled in the 1970s

staffing.status: Staffed from 1939 by one observer who lived at the Kekekabic cabin; no later staffing in sources read

access.note: Site lies in the Boundary Waters wilderness, on the Kekekabic Trail (about 100 people use it per season); no source found on restrictions; no tower remains standing

events.note: Reported completed in January 1937 as a 100-foot tower on the Kawishiwi ranger district; built in the 1930s
Bill Rom signed on to man the tower; a single observer was stationed on site for months at a time

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The January 1937 report and the state list give 100 feet (30.5 m); a later Timberjay article gives 110 feet. The record keeps 100 feet and the story reports both.
kjackson dates the tower to the 1930s; the 1937 report says it was completed by January 1937. The record uses 1937.
The quoted 1937 report names the ranger station as Elk in one transcription (Central US Lookouts) and Ely in another (kjackson). Not used in the story.

notes_for_editor: No removal date found; the record's fate rests on a Minnesota list (probably destroyed or damaged during removal) and a visitor's 1970s account of the tower toppled. The 2011 visitor could not find the tower. Height conflict (100 vs 110 ft) is noted. The FFLA point is for this tower, but the lake is in Lake County per the record's county field; the story does not dispute it. No new photos added; the photo already in the record is a NARA image of the tower (undated in the record).
